cards.explanation: The answer is judgment. God presides in the divine assembly, and among the gods He renders judgment (Psalm 82:1). This is a courtroom scene, friends, and God is the one presiding. The next verses show what He has to say.

The answer is judging unjustly and favoring the wicked. God asks, "How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked?" (Psalm 82:2). Notice He says "How long," so this has been going on a while. A judge who plays favorites is like a scale that always leans the same way. You can't trust the number it gives you.

The answer is the weak and the fatherless. God says, "Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless…" (Psalm 82:3). He tells the assembly to stand up for them, friends. The very next verse keeps going with the weak and needy.

The answer is True. God says, "uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed." (Psalm 82:3). It's the same job said a second way. Defend the weak, and also hold up the rights of the ones being pressed down.

The answer is all the foundations of the earth. The verse says, "all the foundations of the earth are shaken." (Psalm 82:5). Wandering in the darkness and shaken foundations in the same breath. I think that's a house with no light and no floor you can trust, and that's a rough combo.

The answer is gods and sons of the Most High. God says, "I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’" (Psalm 82:6). That's a big title to be handed, bakers. And it makes the verdict in the next verse hit even harder.

The answer is that they will die like mortals. God says, "But like mortals you will die…" (Psalm 82:7). The ones He called gods are told they'll die like mortals. That's a short sentence, friends, but I bet it landed like a dropped tray.

The answer is True. God says, "…and like rulers you will fall." (Psalm 82:7). Two comparisons in one verse. They die like mortals and fall like rulers. A title can sound grand, but it doesn't keep anyone standing.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance." (Psalm 82:8). The ask covers the whole earth, friends. Israel isn't named in this verse at all.

The answer is that all the nations are His inheritance. The psalm says, "…for all the nations are Your inheritance." (Psalm 82:8). That's the reason it gives, friends. The psalm ends by calling God to arise, with all the nations as His.
